AI mathematics and space technology · as of 7 Oct 2026

Space Unlock Tree

What becomes solvable in space technology when AI can do research mathematics on request? Each card is a problem, method, technology or outcome. Each line says one must come before the other. Cards sit in the year they first become credible under the chosen scenario. Move the year to see what has unlocked, through 2035. A card counts as unlocked once its year arrives and its odds for that year are High or Medium. Odds are rated for every year from 2026 to 2035. The year is the earliest credible year, not a forecast date.

    Layers

    Likelihood and trust

    Likelihood, year by year
    Each node records the first year its odds reach Low, Medium and High, so it has a rating for every year from 2026 to 2035. Bars show the rating for the chosen year. Four bars: High (roughly over 70%). Three: Medium (30–70%). Two: Low (10–30%). One: Speculative (under 10%). These are analyst judgments, not computed probabilities.
    Earliest credible year
    The first year the node is credibly achieved: a result proved, a tool in use, a first flight. A card cannot unlock before its prerequisites.
    Trust tier of a premise
    T1 a manuscript only, T2 a manuscript with an outside expert's endorsement, T3 an unchecked Lean proof in the lab's repository, T4 an independent machine check plus an audit of the formal statement. Nothing in the October 2026 release is above T3. Nodes resting on T1 or T2 results are conditional.
    Binding gate
    The slowest thing between the node and reality: cognition, formalization, data, experiment, fabrication, qualification, regulation, capital, launch for SpaceX's own manifest (launch-internal), launch for outside customers (launch-external) or adoption. We assign the gate whose removal would move the node's earliest year the most in the central scenario, and record the runner-up gate beside it.
    Built from a model of nodes and dependencies, researched on 7 October 2026 from the openai/math release, agency and company sources, and 33FG research. Forecasts are scenario judgments, not predictions of record.
